decisions.executionNote: Approach the right-side tube first, lifting into a continuous elbow-up reach and pitching the open gripper toward the tabletop.
Continue the right-arm overhead approach; align the closing jaws across the right tube while preserving elbow-up continuity.
Lower toward the middle of the right tube with the jaws open; refine the near-vertical approach from the wrist view.
Wrist view shows the tube off-center and too far toward the fingertips; translate along and across it and correct yaw before closing.
Bring the cap and tube body into the demonstrated wrist alignment, then close around the upper body. Retention will be checked during lift.
Lift the closed right gripper away from the table and retract slightly; confirm the tube follows before rotating upright.
The right tube follows the gripper. Begin rotating it upright and carrying it above the rack's right-side holes, keeping the grasp closed.
Continue the gradual upright rotation and move over the right rack region with clearance above the plate.
Finish making the tube vertical and pause above a right-side slot to refine horizontal alignment before insertion.
Lower the upright tube toward the right-front rack opening with the grasp closed, stopping short to inspect the tip-to-hole alignment.
Nudge toward the visible opening and lower slowly into the rack, keeping the tube upright and closed in the gripper.
The tube appears to have contacted the plate rather than seated. Lift slightly, correct toward the exposed hole, and retry a gentle vertical descent.
Open over the apparent slot and allow the upright tube to settle, then withdraw slightly to inspect whether it is seated or needs correction.
The tube tipped onto the rack instead of seating. Raise clear and begin a top-down regrasp aligned with its new diagonal orientation.
Replan the regrasp with smaller rotation increments after the joint-continuity rejection, raising and approaching the tube on the rack.
Rotate toward a top-down grasp of the fallen tube, keeping the right gripper on the right half of the rack.
Complete the overhead orientation and center the right jaws on the fallen tube before closing.
Use small translation-only corrections after the continuity guard: lower for reach margin and center the tube between the jaws without further wrist rotation.
Move the open jaws along the fallen tube toward its thicker upper body, with a small yaw correction and a slow descent.
Stop the reach at the guard boundary. Close at the current centered body position, then retract toward the robot to recover arm margin while testing retention.
Retract the closed gripper in much smaller increments from the near-limit configuration, lifting the regrasped tube just clear of the rack.
The regrasped tube follows the fingers. Retract to a safer reach while lifting and slowly turning the tube upright for a better-aligned insertion attempt.
Carry the retained tube toward the right-front rack region while completing its upright rotation with continuous small increments.
Finish the upright orientation, then use the now-visible rack geometry for a more cautious second insertion.
Lower the upright tube vertically toward the right slot, without lateral pushing, and inspect before releasing.
Correct the tube toward the front row rather than the back edge: lift slightly, then shift toward the robot to align with the open right-front hole.
Test the corrected front-row alignment with a slow vertical descent, maintaining the closed upright grasp.
The tube descended with the gripper to the expected seated height. Open and withdraw carefully to verify it remains upright in the rack.
The second release did not remain seated. Clear the right arm and approach a left-side tube, aiming for a higher-body grasp that leaves more tube below the jaws for insertion.
Approach the diagonal tube on the left with open jaws while returning the right arm toward its home pose.
Align the left gripper perpendicular to the diagonal tube and descend toward its upper body; leave the right arm clear.
Refine the left wrist's tube alignment and close around the upper body, leaving the tapered lower section free for insertion.
Corrected the rejected tensor; lift the left tube and retract slightly with the grasp closed while leaving the right arm stationary.
Rotate the retained left tube upright above the rack, targeting a central large opening with more clearance from the edges.
Complete the left tube's upright rotation above the central rack opening, keeping the tube well above the plate before descending.
Corrected the invalid row without compensating for unexecuted motion. Lower toward the central opening with the left grasp closed.
The tube is still retained without visible sliding. Continue a straight, slow descent into the central slot and inspect at insertion height.
The tube slid upward on contact with the plate. Lift clear before making a small correction toward the center of the opening; do not release a blocked tube.
Retry the central opening after the small alignment correction, descending vertically while watching for renewed slipping.
The corrected descent retained the tube. Advance another short distance slowly to account for the earlier grasp slip, watching for contact.
The tube is blocked, possibly in an undersized opening. Lift its tip fully clear and reposition above an adjacent visibly larger opening on the left/back portion of the rack.
Descend vertically over the larger neighboring opening, retaining the tube and stopping before release to inspect seating.
The tip is over the web between holes. Shift slightly toward the exposed large opening and loosen only enough to let the tube settle while the jaws still guide it.
Pause with the jaws slightly open to allow settling into the neighboring large hole, keeping the arm stationary for a clear visual check.
Arrest the tilt, lift the tube, and move its tip toward the clearly exposed large front opening rather than the web between holes.
The tube tilted within the loosened jaws. Keep it closed, lift clear, and compensate its backward lean before another placement.
Lift the tip clear and align it with the clearly exposed large opening to the right in the wrist view, avoiding the front rim.
Make a small wrist-image correction toward the large opening beside the tip, rather than the small front hole, and approach slowly.
The large opening is now directly beneath the tip in the wrist view. Descend vertically with the grasp closed and inspect for seating.
Continue the slow vertical insertion over the aligned large opening; the tube has followed the previous descent without new sliding.
The tip is over the large opening and further descent is blocked at the jaws. Open fully to let the tube settle, then clear the rack for inspection.
The tube has dropped into the large opening with the jaws open. Withdraw clear and inspect its stability while returning the left wrist toward a neutral orientation.
